# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 110 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 110 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_110_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 27 — Concluding Exhortation

**1** After a few days the shepherd came to me and said, "Have I not delivered to you the commandments and the similitudes?" "You have, Lord," I said. **2** "Why then have you not yet fulfilled them? For they are needful for you." "Lord," I said, "I do not know what hinders me — there are so many things; I wait, and I cannot fulfill them." **3** "If then you do not fulfill them, you will lose your salvation; for I was sent to save you. But you have not fulfilled what I said to you. **4** But if you live according to my commandments, you shall be saved; and all who live according to these commandments shall be saved, and they shall have life forever." **5** "Lord," I said, "I will carry out whatever you have commanded me; for I know that you were sent for my salvation." **6** "But these things must be kept — by you and by all who shall believe in the Lord their God and walk in his commandments." **7** And he wrote these commandments and similitudes in a book; and he said to me: "Write these commandments and the similitudes you have heard from me, and also the visions you have seen from the beginning." **8** And so he departed from me; and I wept and prayed to the Lord that he would forgive my former sins; and I besought the Lord to complete what he had shown me through his holy shepherd. **9** And the Lord heard my prayer and granted my petition with words of grace.

---

### Translator's Note
Chapter 110 is the formal literary conclusion of Similitude 9 and the compositional self-statement of the Shepherd as a whole. The shepherd's command to write (v. 7) explains the book Hermas is writing. The weeping and prayer (v. 8) ground the entire elaborate vision in personal piety. SOPHIA follows LOGOS throughout; PNEUMA's "grace and comfort" in v. 9 adds "comfort" not in the Greek.
